roster.name: Commercial LEO Destinations
roster.note: NASA funds several companies to build private stations, planning to become a customer of orbital outposts rather than the operator of one

roster.name: Axiom Station
roster.note: Axiom Space's modules are to attach to the ISS first, then detach to fly free as an independent commercial station before the ISS is retired

roster.name: Orbital Reef
roster.note: a Blue Origin and Sierra Space venture pitched as a 'mixed-use business park' in orbit — research, manufacturing, and tourism

roster.name: Starlab
roster.note: a Voyager and Airbus station designed as a single large free-flyer, aimed at continuous science after the ISS

roster.name: ISS retirement
roster.note: the ISS is to be deorbited around 2030; the commercial stations are meant to be flying before it goes, so human presence in low orbit is never interrupted
